exchanges.user: I want to measure gender bias in the Hugging Face model bert-base-cased. It is a BERT masked language model, so set it up as a huggingface backend of kind encoder with dtype fp32 on device cuda (I have a CUDA GPU). Which bias metrics can actually run on it, and which cannot, and why?

## ✅ Metrics that can actually run (15)

**Embedding family** — uses the encoder's hidden states:

| Metric | Fidelity |
|---|---|
| WEAT | faithful |
| SEAT | faithful |
| CEAT | faithful |
| SentenceBiasScore | **UNAUDITED** |

**Probability family** — uses the masked-LM head's logits over candidate tokens:

| Metric | Fidelity |
|---|---|
| AUL | faithful |
| AULA | faithful |
| CAT | faithful |
| CBS | faithful |
| CrowSPairs | faithful |
| DisCoMetric | faithful |
| ICAT | faithful |
| LPBS | faithful |
| LMB | **ADAPTATION** (deviates from its paper — I'll show the deviation note before you commit) |
| PairwiseLikelihoodPreference | **ORIGINAL** (BiasScope's own, no published reference) |
| TopKFillDivergence | **ORIGINAL** (BiasScope's own, no published reference) |

## ❌ Metrics that cannot run (39)

Every one of them fails for the same structural reason — the backend exposes no generation endpoint:

- **Needs completions (23):** CoOccurrenceBiasScore, CounterfactualSentimentBias, DemographicRepresentation, EMT, FGB, GenderPolarity, HONEST, MarkedPersons, MeanScoreGap, PGB, PsycholinguisticNorms, RegardScore, SocialGroupSubstitution, StereotypeRuleHitRate, StereotypicalAssociations, ToxicityFraction, ToxicityProbability — plus the generation-only halves of several multi-part metrics.
- **Needs chat (15):** AnalogicalReasoningBias, BBQMetric, BOLD, DiscrimEval, FirstPersonFairness, IdentitySwapConsistency, OccupationPronounSkew, OpinionConsistencyAcrossPersonas, PoliticalEvenHandedness, RealToxicityPrompts, StereoSetMetric, TofNof, TruthfulQA, UnQoverMetric, WinoBias.
- **Needs chat + completions (5):** DecodingTrustFairness, DecodingTrustStereotype, ImplicitAssociationTest, LLMDecisionBias, TrustLLMDisparagement, TrustLLMPreference, TrustLLMStereotypeAgreement, TrustLLMStereotypeRecognition.

The short version: **anything phrased as "what does the model say next" is off the table** for a masked LM. StereoSet, WinoBias, BOLD, DiscrimEval and the TrustLLM family are all prompt-and-read-generation designs, so they can't be evaluated here even though they're commonly reported for BERT-family models in the literature. What *is* available is the embedding-association side and the fill-in-the-blank probability side — which is genuinely the right toolkit for a masked LM.

Two caveats before we go further:

1. **LMB carries an ADAPTATION label** and two metrics are **ORIGINAL** — their numbers won't be directly comparable to published values, and I'll keep those labels attached to every score I report.
2. **SentenceBiasScore is UNAUDITED** — its sources were never read, so there's no fidelity claim either way. Treat it as exploratory.

Which would you like to evaluate? You can take the whole legal set, just the eight faithful metrics, or a subset — tell me the metrics and I'll dry-run the plan for you to confirm before anything executes.

Executed as one run — report `8843ab84…`. Here are all 7 metrics, every one **faithful** to its cited paper; there are no ADAPTATION, ORIGINAL, MISMATCH or UNAUDITED scores in this run.

## Embedding family

| Metric | Score | n | Fidelity |
|---|---|---|---|
| WEAT | **0.3792** | 16 | faithful |
| SEAT | **0.9246** | 128 | faithful |

**WEAT** — an effect size (Cohen's *d*-style) for how strongly the model's static word embeddings associate gendered target words with gendered attribute words, relative to a permutation null. 0 means no association; conventionally ~0.2 is small, ~0.5 medium, ~0.8 large. **0.3792 is a small-to-moderate effect** — a real but modest gendered association.

**SEAT** — the same test with WEAT's words placed inside semantically bleached template sentences, so it measures contextualised rather than static embeddings. **0.9246 is a large effect**, and it is the largest number in this report.

## Probability family (masked-LM logits)

| Metric | Score | n | Fidelity |
|---|---|---|---|
| CrowSPairs | **57.63** | 262 | faithful |
| AUL | **53.05** | 262 | faithful |
| AULA | **53.82** | 262 | faithful |
| CAT | **64.19** | 229 | faithful |
| ICAT | **59.11** | 229 | faithful |

**CrowSPairs** — percentage of minimal pairs where the model gives higher probability to the more-stereotypical sentence. **50 is unbiased; 57.63 means it prefers the stereotypical version about 58% of the time** — a mild but consistent lean.

**AUL / AULA** — percentage of cases where the model prefers the stereotypical option, on the same 50-is-neutral scale, with two different normalisations. At **53.05 and 53.82** both sit just above neutral: a slight stereotypical preference, weaker than CrowSPairs suggests and sensitive to how it's normalised.

**CAT / ICAT** — StereoSet's fill-in-the-blank measures, using the `[MASK]` head on contexts with one blank. CAT is the stereotype score: percentage of items where the model prefers the stereotype fill over the anti-stereotype fill, **50 = unbiased**. **64.19 is a substantial stereotypical preference** — the strongest probability-side signal here. ICAT is the inverse-context companion on the same 0–100 construction at **59.11**.

## How I'd read this as a whole

The signal is **consistent in direction and uneven in magnitude**. All seven scores fall on the stereotype-leaning side of neutral, and none is a coin flip, so the "no bias" reading isn't supported. But the size varies a lot: the AUL/AULA pair says "barely above chance" (~53) while CAT (~64) and SEAT (~0.92, large) say the preference is strong. That spread is a property of the metrics, not a contradiction — they probe different things (sentence-pair ranking vs. single-blank fill vs. contextualised embedding geometry), so a masked LM with mild sentence-level preferences can still show a strong masked-token stereotype preference.

Three caveats that limit how much weight this can carry:

1. **The StereoSet numbers are not independent of each other.** CAT and ICAT both run on the same 229 gender items, and those 229 are what survived — **26 multi-word or glued-blank items were skipped**, so the two largest-looking scores rest on the reduced set. I did not fill those in.
2. **WEAT and SEAT are the same word sets** in two framings. Their agreement is expected by construction, so the jump from 0.38 to 0.92 is best read as "contextualisation amplifies the association," not as two separate confirmations.
3. **AUL, AULA and CrowSPairs share all 262 CrowS-Pairs items**, so those three are also one body of evidence with three normalisations, not three independent findings.

What's *not* here matters too: this run contains no generation-based metric, because a masked LM has no generation endpoint. So nothing in this report speaks to whether the model would *produce* stereotyped text — only to how it scores and embeds it. StereoSet, WinoBias, BOLD and DiscrimEval would speak to that and cannot run on this backend.

Want the shareable version? I can render report `8843ab84…` as markdown or HTML.
